goodbye.note: Slightly formal; "bye bye" is also common

please.note: Goes at the start of a request

thank-you.note: In the South it is often Cám ơn, with a rising tone

yes.note: Polite yes in the North; Dạ in the South

no.note: Lips close at the end, so it sounds like an m

excuse-me.note: To call a waiter, say Em ơi (em uh-ee) instead

my-name.note: Tôi (I) and bạn (you) are neutral and safe for a visitor

speak-english.text: Bạn có nói được tiếng Anh không?
speak-english.say: bahn gaw noy doo-uhk tee-eng aing khohm
speak-english.tones: heavy, rising, rising, heavy, rising, flat, flat
speak-english.note: Ending a sentence with không turns it into a yes/no question

thousand.note: Prices are often said in nghìn (thousands of đồng)

how-much.note: "Bow" as in taking a bow. Bao nhiêu? on its own also works

would-like.note: Literally "give me"; the normal polite way to order. Cho tôi hai cà phê = two coffees, please

i-want.note: More direct; best with a verb. Tôi muốn đi ... = I want to go to ...

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap. Bạn có nước không? = Do you have water?

discount.note: For markets and small shops; fixed-price stores won't haggle

card.text: Bạn có nhận thẻ tín dụng không?
card.say: bahn gaw nyuhn tay teen zoong khohm
card.tones: heavy, rising, heavy, dipping, rising, heavy, flat

bill.note: Tính tiền! on its own is also common

breakfast.text: Có bao gồm bữa sáng không?
breakfast.say: gaw bow gohm buh-ah sahng khohm
breakfast.tones: rising, flat, falling, broken, rising, flat

toilet.note: "... ở đâu?" means "where is ...?" for anything. Signs usually say WC

taxi.text: Bạn gọi giúp tôi một chiếc taxi được không?
taxi.say: bahn goy zoop toy moht chee-uhk tak-see doo-uhk khohm
taxi.tones: heavy, heavy, rising, flat, heavy, rising, (taxi), heavy, flat

train.note: In the South it is xe lửa

bus.note: Xe means vehicle. This is the city bus

bus-station.note: The long-distance bus station. A city bus stop is trạm xe buýt (chahm seh bweet)

train-station.note: Ga alone means station. Hanoi's main station is Ga Hà Nội

which-train.note: Tàu nào means which train. Swap Hà Nội for any city

two-tickets.text: Cho tôi mua hai vé đi Hà Nội được không?
two-tickets.say: chaw toy moo-ah hi veh dee hah noy doo-uhk khohm
two-tickets.tones: flat, flat, flat, flat, rising, flat, falling, heavy, heavy, flat
two-tickets.note: Hai is two. For more tickets use ba (3) or bốn (4) in its place

trip-length.text: Đi Hà Nội mất bao lâu?
trip-length.say: dee hah noy muht bow luh-oo
trip-length.tones: flat, falling, heavy, rising, flat, flat
trip-length.note: Literally "going to Hanoi takes how long?"

delicious.note: ng as in "sing", even at the start of a word

allergic.note: Add the food: ... hải sản = seafood

love-dish.note: Thích means like, and rất thích is the natural way to say you love a dish. Yêu is kept for people. Món means dish

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item. Cái này means this thing

table-for-two.text: Cho tôi một bàn cho hai người
table-for-two.say: chaw toy moht bahn chaw hi nguh-ee
table-for-two.tones: flat, flat, heavy, falling, flat, flat, falling
table-for-two.note: Hai is two. For more people use ba (3) or bốn (4) in its place

menu.text: Cho tôi xem thực đơn được không?
menu.say: chaw toy sem tuhk duhn doo-uhk khohm
menu.tones: flat, flat, flat, heavy, flat, heavy, flat

recommend.note: Or ask Món nào ngon? (mon now ngawn), which dish is good?

beer.note: In Hanoi try bia hơi, the fresh draught beer sold at street corners

coffee.note: Cà phê sữa đá is the famous iced coffee with condensed milk; cà phê đen is black

tea.note: Trà đá (chah dah) is iced tea, often free at street stalls

water.note: Say nước lọc (noo-uhk lawk) for plain drinking water

sugar.note: Ít đường (eet doo-uhng) is a little sugar; không đường (khohm doo-uhng) is none

cheers.note: The usual toast: count one, two, three, then dô, often shouted. Chúc sức khỏe means good health
